source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC official Measles surveillance pages, case count tables, and outbreak investigation reports for the United States covering January–March 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary national public health authority for US measles surveillance and publishes weekly/monthly case counts, outbreak summaries, and MMWR reports that are the gold standard for confirmed case and death data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department pages (all 50 states + DC + territories) reporting Measles cases, outbreaks, or alerts during 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments report subnational case counts, outbreak investigations, and exposure notifications that are essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MMWR (Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report) articles published in 2025 Q1 reporting US measles cases, outbreaks, or surveillance summaries.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR is CDC's primary peer-reviewed surveillance publication and frequently contains extractable case counts, outbreak descriptions, and epidemiological data with evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO and PAHO situation reports or disease surveillance bulletins covering US measles cases in Q1 2025 for independent cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and PAHO independently aggregate US measles data and can serve as held-back validation sources to verify CDC-reported totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured public health databases (e.g., Project Tycho, HealthData.gov, CDC Wonder) containing US measles case data for 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide machine-readable case counts that can be compared against extracted records for numeric validation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition pages and measles surveillance methodology documents to support count semantics interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected case definitions is critical for correctly populating cases_confirmed, cases_probable, and cases_suspected fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature published in 2025 describing US measles epidemiology, outbreak investigations, or vaccination coverage gaps relevant to Q1 2025.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature provides case definitions, epidemiological context, and may contain extractable case series data for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear geographic scope, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that mix cumulative annual totals with Q1-specific counts, or that serve dual collection/validation roles, require human adjudication before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC and state/local health departments are the authoritative sources for US measles case counts, outbreak reports, and death data. CDC publishes national surveillance summaries and MMWR outbreak reports. State health departments provide subnational breakdowns essential for locality-level data.

WHO Disease Outbreak News, WHO measles surveillance data, and PAHO EpiAlerts independently report US measles cases and can validate CDC-reported totals. WHO IHR notifications may also contain US measles data.
Project Tycho, CDC Wonder, HealthData.gov, and similar open data portals may contain structured US measles surveillance data for 2025 that enables numeric cross-validation of extracted records.

MMWR articles, Emerging Infectious Diseases, and other peer-reviewed journals may publish US measles outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for Q1 2025, providing extractable case data and case definitions.

Reputable news outlets (AP, Reuters, NPR, ProPublica) and public health news services (CIDRAP, Helen Branswell/STAT) may report early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and death reports before official sources publish summaries.

source_planning_risks.risk: A source intended for validation may leak into collection if roles are not enforced during later discovery.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Keep validation-reserved sources separate until evaluation.

source_planning_risks.risk: Cumulative, annual, newly reported, and suspected counts may be mixed across source categories.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Require evidence quotes and count-semantics fields.
